newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-BARMASAI IN WORLD CROSS COUNTRY AFTER ALL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BARMASAI IN WORLD CROSS COUNTRY AFTER ALL.

text.p: Kenyan Bernard Barmasai is to run in the world cross country championships in Turin, Italy, on Sunday after all.

Barmasai, who is second in the season-long International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) world cross challenge series, originally said he would not compete in the championship and did not take part in the Kenyan trials last month.
"We changed our minds after his last race in Europe last month," said Caroline Feith, a spokeswoman for his Dutch agent Jos Hermans, speaking by telephone from the Netherlands.
"After all there is a lot of money at stake and he believes he can place in the top five. So we asked the Kenyan federation to include him."
The world cross challenge, which culminates in the world cross country championships, has a first prize of $25,000 while the championship itself has a first prize of $40,000.
Kenyan athletics officials had previously said that runners had to compete in their trials to be included in the squad going to Turin.
Kenyan teams have won the senior men's race at the world championship for the last 11 years and provided the individual men's winner since 1992.
